exercise.instruction_pt: Listen. How certain is the speaker?
exercise.listen: I wouldn't go so far as to say it's a failure, but the early numbers are, let's say, less than encouraging.
options: She thinks it's a complete failure.
She thinks the results so far are disappointing.
She is very optimistic.
exercise.explanation_pt: "I wouldn't go so far as to say" rejects the strongest claim, and "less than encouraging" is understatement for disappointing.

exercise.instruction_pt: Listen. What does the speaker really think of the hotel?
exercise.listen: Oh, the hotel was charming. Nothing says luxury like a cold shower and a view of the car park.
options: He loved it.
He was disappointed with it.
He thought it was expensive but good.
exercise.explanation_pt: "Nothing says luxury like a cold shower" is sarcasm: he means the opposite.

exercise.instruction_pt: Listen. Who is most likely speaking to whom?
exercise.listen: Further to our conversation earlier, I'd be grateful if you could confirm the revised figures at your earliest convenience.
options: A teenager talking to a friend.
A professional writing or speaking to a client or partner.
A parent talking to a child.
exercise.explanation_pt: "Further to", "I'd be grateful if" and "at your earliest convenience" are typical of formal business register.

exercise.instruction_pt: Listen and sum up the speaker's point in one short sentence.
exercise.listen: The flights are cheaper in March, the weather's milder, and the museums aren't packed with tourists. If you ask me, there's no contest.
accepted: So March is the best time to go
In short, it's better to go in March
Basically, you should go in March
In a nutshell, March is the best option
So you think we should travel in March
So March is better in every way
The bottom line is that March is the best time to go
So it's best to go in March

commonErrors.correction_en: So March is the best time to go.
So it's best to go in March.

exercise.instruction_pt: Listen. Your colleague is upset. Acknowledge how they feel before anything else.
exercise.listen: I stayed late every night this month, and nobody even said thank you.
accepted: That must be really frustrating
I can see why you're upset
I can understand why you're frustrated
That sounds really frustrating
I'm sorry, that must be really disheartening
I can see why you feel unappreciated
I completely understand how you feel
That's not fair on you. I'd be upset too
I hear you. That must be frustrating

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Calm down" tends to sound dismissive. Acknowledge the feeling first.

commonErrors.correction_en: I completely understand how you feel.

exercise.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Eu tendo a achar que a culpa não é só dele."
accepted: I'm inclined to think it's not only his fault
I tend to think it's not just his fault
I'm inclined to think it isn't entirely his fault
I tend to think he's not the only one to blame
I'm inclined to think he's not solely to blame
I tend to think it's not all his fault
I'd be inclined to think it's not only his fault

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "A culpa é dele" is "it's his fault". "Guilt" is the feeling of being guilty (culpa moral).
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm inclined to think it's not only his fault.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Tend to" is followed by the base form: "tend to think".
commonErrors.correction_en: I tend to think it's not just his fault.

exercise.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English, with phrasal verbs: "Eles recusaram a proposta, então tivemos que bolar outra coisa."
accepted: They turned down the proposal, so we had to come up with something else
They turned the proposal down, so we had to come up with something else
They turned it down, so we had to come up with something else
They turned down the offer, so we had to come up with something else
They turned down our proposal, so we had to come up with something different
They rejected the proposal, so we had to come up with something else

commonErrors.explanation_pt: To reject an offer is "turn down"; "turn off" is for switching off a device.
commonErrors.correction_en: They turned down the proposal, so we had to come up with something else.
They turned down the proposal, so we had to come up with something else.

exercise.instruction_pt: Make this feedback more constructive and say it: "Your report is too long."
accepted: It might be worth making the report a bit shorter
It might be worth cutting the report down a little
Have you considered shortening the report?
The report could be a bit more concise
I think the report could be shorter
Maybe the report could be a little more concise
It might help to trim the report a bit
Perhaps you could make the report more concise

commonErrors.explanation_pt: That's still a blunt judgement. Turn it into a suggestion: "It might be worth..." or "Have you considered...?".
commonErrors.correction_en: It might be worth making the report a bit shorter.
It might be worth making the report a bit shorter.

exercise.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Só quando o avião decolou é que percebi que tinha deixado as chaves em casa."
accepted: It was only when the plane took off that I realised I'd left my keys at home
It was only when the plane took off that I realized I had left my keys at home
It wasn't until the plane took off that I realised I'd left my keys at home
Only when the plane took off did I realise I'd left my keys at home
I only realised I'd left my keys at home when the plane took off
It was only when the plane took off that I realised I'd left the keys at home

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Em casa" is "at home", with no article.
commonErrors.correction_en: It was only when the plane took off that I realised I'd left my keys at home.
It was only when the plane took off that I realised I'd left my keys at home.

exercise.instruction_pt: Answer in one or two minutes, as if in a debate.
exercise.prompt_en: Some people argue that working from home is killing company culture. To what extent do you agree?
guidelines_pt: State a clear, hedged position: "I'd argue that..." or "To some extent...".
Support it with a reason and an example.
Concede a point: "I'll grant you that...".

exercise.instruction_pt: Match the false friends with their real meanings.
You're chairing a meeting and someone raises an unrelated issue. What do you say?
options: Let's park that for now and come back to it later.
Let's bring that forward.
Let's take that on board immediately.
exercise.explanation_pt: "Park" an issue = leave it for later. "Bring forward" means to move something to an earlier time.

exercise.instruction_pt: Match each expression with its meaning.

pairs.pt: não dar valor, dar como certo

exercise.instruction_pt: "Could you put me in touch with your sales director?" means...
options: Could you call your sales director for me right now?
Could you introduce me to your sales director?
Could you send me your sales director's CV?
exercise.explanation_pt: "Put someone in touch with" = connect them, introduce them.

exercise.instruction_pt: Which word describes humour delivered with a completely serious face?
options: deadpan
slapstick
cheesy
exercise.explanation_pt: "Deadpan" = said with no expression. "Slapstick" is physical comedy; "cheesy" means corny (brega).

exercise.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
exercise.sentence: Only when I got home ___ I realise my wallet was missing.
accepted: did

commonErrors.explanation_pt: After "Only when..." at the start, invert subject and auxiliary: "did I realise".
commonErrors.correction_en: Only when I got home did I realise my wallet was missing.

exercise.instruction_pt: Complete with the correct form of "add".
exercise.sentence: It might be worth ___ a short summary at the start.
accepted: adding

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Worth" is followed by the -ing form: "worth adding".
commonErrors.correction_en: It might be worth adding a short summary at the start.

exercise.instruction_pt: Which sentence is correct?
options: The honesty is the most important quality in a leader.
Honesty is the most important quality in a leader.
A honesty is the most important quality in a leader.
exercise.explanation_pt: General abstract nouns take no article in English: "Honesty is...".

exercise.instruction_pt: Put the words in the correct order.
accepted: We'll have to put it off until next week

exercise.instruction_pt: Complete the formal sentence with one word.
exercise.sentence: We look forward to ___ with you on this project.
accepted: working

commonErrors.explanation_pt: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so use -ing: "working".
commonErrors.correction_en: We look forward to working with you on this project.
